To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

miR- 10a is a marker of Treg but inhibition of expression in vitro or genetic ablation does not affect FoxP3 expression in Treg or the capacity of conventional CD4+ T cells to induce expression of FoxP3.
microRNA-1oa (miR-1oa) is selectively expressed in regulatory T cells, but inhibition of miR-1oa by antagomiR or genetic ablation does not affect regulatory T cell development or function.
MicroRNA-10a is a marker for regulatory T cells (Tregs) but inhibition of its expression does not affect the number and phenotype or stability of Tregs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of microRNAs (miRs) in regulatory T cells (Tregs) which are crucial for their function and stability.
the role of microRNA-10 (miR- 10a) in Treg stability and function.
the identification and characterization of microRNAs in regulatory T cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miR- 10a is a marker for FoxP3+ Treg but not for FoxP3 expression per se.
miR- 10a is not required for FoxP3 expression but may contribute to the stability of Treg.
miR- 10a is a marker for Treg but is not a key regulator of Treg stability or function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
miR- 10a does not play a critical role in the development or function of Treg.
miR- 10a expression in Treg is associated with stability and function of the cells but is dispensable for Treg differentiation and function.
miR- 10a does not play a role in Treg stability or function in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Treg-specific expression of miR- 10a is not required for TGFβ-mediated induction of FoxP3 or for Treg development.
miR- 10a is selectively and constitutively expressed in Treg and that miR-1 0a is required for the maintenance of the Treg phenotype in vitro
miR-1010a does not seem to be required for Treg function and stability.
